name: Saint Antoninus
history: A Dominican friar of Florence who became its archbishop and lived as poor as his flock. He helped found the friary of San Marco, gave away almost everything he had, set up a confraternity to help families ashamed to beg, and wrote a great work of moral theology that dealt with trade, money and the just price.
life: Antonino Pierozzi, son of a Florentine notary, entered the Dominicans at Fiesole as a teenager, under the influence of Blessed John Dominici and his strict reform. He was prior of several friaries, and with the help of Cosimo de’ Medici founded San Marco in Florence, where Fra Angelico painted the cells. He served as a theologian at the Council of Florence. In 1446 Pope Eugene IV named him archbishop of Florence, and he accepted only under obedience. His household was tiny and his clothes poor; he sold his own goods in famine and plague, visited his parishes on foot, and was known for settling disputes. He founded the Buonomini di San Martino to help the ‘shamefaced poor’, families fallen into need who were too proud to beg; it still exists. His Summa of moral theology was one of the first to treat economic life seriously. He died in 1459.
prayerTo: Saint Antoninus, you governed your city as a shepherd and lived as a poor friar. Pray for Florence, for bishops and civic leaders, and for those who work in trade and finance. Help me to be honest in all my dealings and generous to those who are ashamed to ask for help. Amen.
penance: Help someone quietly today who would be embarrassed to ask, without letting them know it came from you. Review one of your financial habits in the light of justice.
meditation: He cared especially for the poor who hid their poverty. Who around you is struggling in silence?
prayer: O Lord, may the merits of St. Antoninus, Your Confessor and Bishop, help us; and just as we praise You for the wonders You have wrought in him, so may we glory in Your mercy toward us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
